key_insight: A passive reduced-order sloshing model combines meniscus curvature, viscous losses and contact-line hysteresis to predict low-gravity tank dynamics more accurately.
engineering_relevance: Faster-than-real-time simulation of coupled spacecraft motion and sloshing can support control analyses that account for uncertain damping.
method: Port-Hamiltonian formulation with curvature-aware inertia and restoring operators.
Convex dissipation potential for bulk, Stokes-layer and contact-line losses.
Analytical propagation between contact-line stick-slip events.
evidence_signal: Across 42 drop-tower and ground measurements, curvature correction reduced RMS frequency error from 24% to 4%; a calibrated hysteresis width yielded 11–35% normalised force errors in additional MODE tests versus 149–208% for an ideal pinned line.
watch_item: Uncertain wetting and residual response discrepancies warrant damping ranges rather than a single nominal value in spacecraft control analyses.
paper_title: A curvature-corrected port-Hamiltonian reduced-order model for dissipative sloshing with contact-line hysteresis in low-gravity tanks
